summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for IV diuresis prior to a scheduled right heart catheterization to assess pulmonary artery pressures for liver transplant eligibility. He had recently completed treatment for Acinetobacter bacteremia, which led to removal of his tunneled catheter and placement of a PICC. During this admission, he received IV furosemide for fluid overload, underwent a therapeutic paracentesis removing 1.25 liters of ascites, and had a new tunneled catheter successfully placed. Right heart catheterization showed borderline normal pulmonary pressures with slight improvement, confirming no contraindication to transplant. His diarrhea, attributed to Remodulin, remained stable. He was discharged home with instructions to restart home diuretics, continue all transplant-related medications, and follow up with the liver team for ongoing management.
